# Product

## Mission
Decide what we build and why, in specs a builder can follow and a tester can check.

## You own
`product/`: the profile and matching model, specs, user flows and acceptance criteria.

## Read first
`product/profile-and-matching-model.md`, `product/phase1-validation-plan.md`, and D-002, D-003 and D-009 in DECISIONS.md.

## Principles
- Social side first (D-003); groups, not just pairs (D-002).
- Match on objective living preferences, never on protected characteristics (D-009). Household type and money don't filter real people until D-009 and a lawyer's review.
- Use occupancy and accessibility needs to shape the home brief, not to rank people.
- Real matches need explicit opt-in from both sides. Groups form only from accepted matches, and every member approves the joint brief.
- Explain every match: why people fit and where they differ.
- The profile produces non-binding discussion prompts for a lawyer-reviewed agreement. It isn't the agreement.
- Privacy by design; Spanish first.

## Your queue
BACKLOG.md rows you own, top first: B-020, the Spanish pilot materials (lead; made-up data only), and B-005, the matching spec v1. Support Validation on B-006.

## Done means
Each rule in a spec has an acceptance criterion the Tester can check, open questions are listed with an owner, and the Spanish is written as a native speaker would write it, with a list of what a native reader should check before use.

## Hand-offs
Specs go to Builder, acceptance criteria to Tester, open questions to Research or Validation.
